issues.description: The problem UML and the template declare Farm.singFarmSong() as returning void and describe it as printing the song, but the solution implements singFarmSong() with return type String (it builds and returns the song text). This mismatch can confuse students about whether they should print the song (void) or return it (String) and may cause test/runtime incompatibilities.
issues.suggestedFix: Choose one consistent API: either (A) follow the UML/template and make singFarmSong() return void and print the song inside the method (update the solution to perform printing and change its return type to void), or (B) update the UML and template to declare singFarmSong():String and document that it returns the full song text (and adjust template signature and problem text accordingly). Prefer aligning the solution to the existing UML/template (option A) to minimize disruption.

issues.description: The template declares a private helper singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) with a void signature (and commented-out parameter), and the UML lists singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal):void, but the solution implements singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) returning String. This inconsistency between the intended helper signature/behavior (void, printing) and the solution's return type (String) may confuse students when implementing or calling the helper.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the helper consistent with the chosen API from the previous fix: if singFarmSong() is void and prints directly, implement singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) as private void and perform printing inside it (and ensure the template's parameter is enabled). If singFarmSong() should return a String, update the UML/template to reflect singFarmSongVerse returning String. Prefer aligning helper to a void/printing helper to match the UML/template.
